Examples: [Fix] attention: Fix KV cache indexing; [Perf] [AMD] flash-attn: Optimize decode performance. -->

This PR co-work with mono patch: https://github.com/sgl-project/sgl-amd-mono/pull/13

## Motivation

<!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. -->

The AMD monokernel backend runs the tail of each Kimi-K3 MoE layer as one persistent launch: o_proj, the attention-TP all-reduce, the MLP attention-residual seam and the MoE. For that the attention has to stop at its TP-local output and hand it over. Today both Kimi-K3 attention classes run o_proj inline, so there is no point to stop at.

That backend is sgl-project/sgl-amd-mono. It loads through the `sglang.srt.plugins` entry point and is selected with `--monokernel-backend amd`. SGLang needs nothing else for it: `install_monokernel_forward` swaps the whole model forward (`srt/monokernels/runtime.py`), so the kernels, the spec and its registration all live in the plugin. This method is the one thing the plugin cannot reach from outside, which is why it is the only change here.

## Modifications

<!-- Detail the changes made in this pull request. -->

`forward_gated_core()` on `KimiK3DeltaAttention` and `KimiK3MLAAttention`: the TP-local attention output after the output gate, before o_proj. The caller owns o_proj and the attention-TP reduction it carries, so `o_proj(forward_gated_core(x)) == forward(x)`.

- `KimiK3DeltaAttention`: a plain extract. `forward()` now calls the new method and keeps the o_proj tail; the moved body is unchanged.
- `KimiK3MLAAttention`: the MLA cores reach o_proj from several places, so the split rides on the instance-level wrapper that already applies the output gate. `forward_gated_core()` arms a one-slot sink, runs `forward()`, and takes the tensor the wrapper hands back instead of running o_proj.

Three guards on the MLA path, because it is the one that can go wrong quietly and has no in-tree caller to exercise it:

- the sink holds one tensor, so o_proj being reached twice in one forward raises instead of silently returning the first;
- a quantized o_proj input raises. On ROCm the MLA core quantizes what it hands o_proj when o_proj's weights are MXFP4 or block-scale fp8 (`forward_mla_rocm.py:325,351`), and the output gate is skipped along with it, so there is no gated bf16 tensor to hand back. Every rank quantizes alike, so this raises on all of them rather than splitting the TP group;
- the returned width is asserted against the head count the core actually ran with times `v_head_dim`, so a config that does not land on the expected width fails at the split rather than inside the kernel. The head count is recorded in the wrapper rather than read after `forward()` returns, because decode-time context parallelism lowers `num_local_heads` for the length of the core and restores it on the way out.

The standard path is unchanged: `forward()` produces what it did before.

## Accuracy Tests

<!-- If this pull request affects model outputs (e.g., changes to the kernel or model forward code), provide accuracy test results. -->

8 x MI355X, TP8 / DCP1, FP8 KV cache, DSpark block size 7. `/data-models/Kimi-K3`, GSM8K 200 questions, `--parallel 2`:

| | Accuracy |
|---|---:|
| This branch, no monokernel backend | 0.990 |
| This branch, `--monokernel-backend amd` | 0.985 |

With the backend on, the launch consumes `forward_gated_core`'s output on all 92 MoE layers, and the plugin's kernel checks put the layer output at cos 0.999994 against SGLang's ops with o_proj and the reduce run separately. That is the equivalence this PR claims, measured through the caller.

The numbers above were taken on `e5274752a8`. The branch has since been rebased onto `8e7601ae4a` and the extract re-verified there mechanically (below); the accuracy run was not repeated.


## Speed Tests and Profiling

<!-- If this pull request impacts inference speed, provide benchmarking and profiling results. -->

- [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).

- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [ ] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

## Review and Merge Process

2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers.
3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so.

+    # Set by forward_gated_core() for the length of one forward; the gated
+    # o_proj wrapper below writes the pre-o_proj tensor here instead of
+    # running o_proj. One slot, so a second forward inside the first is an
+    # error rather than a silently dropped result. _core_heads records the
+    # head count the core ran with, which decode-time context parallelism
+    # lowers for the length of the core and restores on the way out.
+    _core_sink: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None
+    _core_heads: int = 0
+    _core_wanted: bool = False
+
     def __init__(
         self,
         config,
@@ -2299,6 +2337,26 @@ def _gated_o_proj_forward(x, *args, **kwargs):
                     # Even a skipped gate must close its capture branch.
                     torch.cuda.current_stream().wait_stream(self._gate_pending_stream)
                     self._gate_pending_stream = None
+                if self._core_wanted:
+                    # forward_gated_core(): hand the gated TP-local output back
+                    # and skip o_proj, whose GEMM and attention-TP reduction
+                    # belong to the caller. The MLA cores reach o_proj from
+                    # several places and only unpack a 2-tuple from it.
+                    if isinstance(x, tuple):
+                        # A quantized o_proj makes the core quantize its input,
+                        # and the gate above is skipped along with it.
+                        raise RuntimeError(
+                            "forward_gated_core: o_proj's input is quantized, so "
+                            "there is no gated bf16 output to hand back"
+                        )
+                    if self._core_sink is not None:
+                        raise RuntimeError(
+                            "forward_gated_core: o_proj was reached twice in one "
+                            "forward; the caller would get the first output only"
+                        )
+                    self._core_sink = x
+                    self._core_heads = self.num_local_heads
+                    return x, None
                 return _orig_o_proj_forward(x, *args, **kwargs)
 
             self.o_proj.forward = _gated_o_proj_forward
@@ -2362,6 +2420,49 @@ def forward(
             positions, hidden_states, forward_batch, zero_allocator, **kwargs
         )
 
+    def forward_gated_core(
+        self,
+        *,
+        hidden_states: torch.Tensor,
+        positions: torch.Tensor,
+        forward_batch: ForwardBatch,
+        zero_allocator: BumpAllocator,
+        **kwargs,
+    ) -> torch.Tensor:
+        """The TP-local attention output after the output gate, before o_proj.
+
+        Shape is ``[num_tokens, num_local_heads * v_head_dim]``. o_proj is left
+        to the caller, which also owns the attention-TP reduction that o_proj
+        would do: ``o_proj(forward_gated_core(x)) == forward(x)``. That holds
+        while o_proj is a plain RowParallelLinear; the SP-MoE and fused
+        all-reduce wraps installed on it are both out of the caller's reach,
+        so a caller must refuse those configurations. A fused decode kernel
+        folds o_proj into a larger launch, so it needs the attention to stop
+        here.
+
+        o_proj is called from inside the DeepseekV2AttentionMLA cores, so the
+        split point is the same instance-level wrapper that applies the gate.
+        """
+        assert self.use_output_gate, "forward_gated_core needs the gated o_proj wrapper"
+        assert not self._core_wanted, "forward_gated_core is not re-entrant"
+        self._core_wanted, self._core_sink = True, None
+        try:
+            self.forward(
+                positions, hidden_states, forward_batch, zero_allocator, **kwargs
+            )
+            core, heads = self._core_sink, self._core_heads
+        finally:
+            self._core_wanted, self._core_sink = False, None
+        if core is None:
+            # An empty batch, or a core that returned without calling o_proj.
+            raise RuntimeError("MLA forward returned without reaching o_proj")
+        want = heads * self.v_head_dim
+        assert core.shape[-1] == want, (
+            f"forward_gated_core: o_proj input is {core.shape[-1]} wide, "
+            f"heads * v_head_dim is {want}"
+        )
+        return core
+
